terms.meaning: A fingerprint of the reviewed plan, so the commit can confirm it matches what was reviewed.
An old evidence quote that was switched off and must not be restored.
A fingerprint computed from data, used to detect changes.
A standard text layout of data so that the same data always gives the same fingerprint.

sections.name: File setup, hash
sections.title: Setup and content hash
sections.what: Loads libraries and defines a helper that makes a fingerprint of any value so that a later check can detect changes.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fingerprint lets the script prove a dry run and a commit see the same data.
sections.watch_out: The fingerprint depends on a stable text form of the data, so changing that form changes all fingerprints.

sections.name: definitions
sections.title: Definitions of the repairs
sections.what: Lists the specific evidence repairs: each entry names a project, a field, the number, the currency, the publisher, the date, the exact quote, and the scope the quote supports.
sections.why: The scope text says what the quote does and does not prove, so the repair does not overstate a source.
sections.watch_out: The quotes must match the captured page exactly, or the check fails before any write.

sections.name: reasons, live
sections.title: Reasons for unresolved fields
sections.what: Gives a plain reason for each project whose stored value could not be supported by a source.
sections.why: These reasons are carried into the report so the owner can see why a field was not repaired.
sections.watch_out: Reasons are typed by hand, so they can go out of date when sources change.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Verify mode and dry-run plan
sections.what: In verify mode, checks committed repairs through the live detail page. Otherwise, builds the plan: each repair is marked as adding evidence or as no change, and it finds stored values that still lack support.
sections.why: Likely reason: the plan must be reviewed before any write, so it is built without writing.
sections.watch_out: Verify mode needs the login secret and the preview domain set, or it stops early.

sections.name: main: if
sections.title: Commit and report
sections.what: When committed, checks the approved fingerprint, stores each quote with a strong anchor, logs each change, confirms no project values changed, and writes the report file.
sections.why: The assertions make the commit stop if any project value changed unexpectedly.
sections.watch_out: The committed report file is never overwritten; a new prefix is needed for a new write batch.

summary: Reconciles the links between Scan projects and their evidence. It changes evidence only, never project values or retired quotes, and it commits only when given the digest of a reviewed no-write plan.
purpose: It fixes evidence links for Scan projects while keeping project figures unchanged, so a reviewer can approve the exact plan before anything is written.
why: The file header states these safety rules, and the digest check makes sure the committed change is the one that was reviewed.
how: Only the setup is visible in this excerpt. It loads the database and helpers, checks the report prefix, and sets up a fingerprint function for data. The remaining steps are not shown here.
inputs: Command line options, including an optional --report-prefix and the --commit option that takes a plan digest. It also uses the artifacts/api-server/data/evidence-repair folder and the database.
outputs: Not visible in this excerpt beyond the setup. The header implies report output and evidence changes.
risks: The header states the safety rules, but the code that enforces them is not in this excerpt, so they cannot be confirmed from here.
debug: If the run stops on the prefix check, the prefix may contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Other debugging needs the rest of the file.
